description: Baseline: deterministic selection benchmark over 242 real evaluated bundles (58 missed-pair, 137 noise-pair labels) replayed through postProcessCandidates.

asi.hypothesis: baseline measurement
asi.benchmark: bun bench/ranking-bench.ts replays frozen real candidate pools through postProcessCandidates and scores top-3 vs human missed/noise labels
asi.ground_truth: human frontmatter missed[]/noise[] from projects/kamil sherpa-evaluations (436 evals joined to 1068 traces)
asi.limitation: upstream_miss_rate=0.93 means 93% of human-labeled missed paths never entered the candidate pool; ranking cannot fix those, so the loop targets noise leakage + top-3 placement
asi.dev_split: 20% hold-out by bundleId hash, monitoring only
asi.next_action_hint: attack noise_leak_rate=0.47 with general junk-path and focus-aware suppression rules; 65 leaks across 52 unique sources, 34 uncovered by obvious junk patterns

description: Add general machine-junk path patterns to global noise filter (caches, Go module cache, .ssh, node_modules, agent session dumps, .semgrep, logs/).

asi.hypothesis: Machine-junk paths (generic caches, Android SDK cache, Go module cache, .ssh, node_modules, agent session dumps, .semgrep state, logs/ dirs) leak into top-3 as noise and can be filtered globally without harming recall.
asi.generality: all patterns are tool/ecosystem-generic, none fixture-specific
asi.remaining_leaks: 52 unique leak sources at baseline; uncovered ones are focus-dependent artifacts (kb://journal, surreal://archivist-note, url_reference, bare directory routes, .pi/sherpa.config.json) needing focus-aware suppression next
asi.next_action_hint: add focus-aware suppression for low-value artifact classes: historical memory (kb://journal) and surreal archivist notes when history not requested, url_reference when web not planned, bare directory/route candidates

description: Focus-gate Sherpa self-artifacts (pi extensions, loops, sherpa traces) with hard filter + penalty — regressed label_loss.

asi.discovery: the same source can be a missed label in one bundle and a noise label in another, so self-artifact sources are genuinely relevant for some prompts
asi.failure: hard postProcessCandidates filter was too aggressive: missed_hit_rate fell 0.724->0.690 (lost 2 of 58 missed pairs) while noise_leak only improved 0.438->0.431
asi.hypothesis: Sherpa/Pi-agent self-artifacts (extension code, loops, traces) crowd out project context on unrelated prompts and should be focus-gated.
asi.next_action_hint: retry with soft ranking penalty only (drop the hard filter) so self-artifacts can still surface when nothing better exists

description: Soft self-artifact ranking penalty without hard filter — no metric change.

asi.hypothesis: soft self-artifact penalty (-1.2) without hard filter should demote self-artifacts below project context while keeping them available
asi.result: metric identical to best (0.7138) — penalty produced zero change in top-3 membership, so the leaked self-artifacts were already below the correspondence threshold or had no competing candidates in their pools
asi.next_action_hint: self-artifact demotion is a dead end on this fixture; pivot to curiosity://knowledge-gaps (6 leak instances), url_reference suppression when web not requested (6), and surreal_memory archivist notes (3)

description: Suppress redundant URL echoes already present in the prompt and focus-gate surreal archivist notes.

asi.discovery: removing redundant/off-topic candidates also promoted known-missed items into top-3, so recall and precision improved together
asi.generality: both rules are principled: (1) a URL already typed in the prompt is redundant context, (2) surreal archivist notes need the same focus gating already applied to research/historical memory
asi.hypothesis: Two artifact classes are pure noise on unrelated prompts: url_reference items that merely echo a URL already in the focus, and surreal_memory archivist notes when the prompt is not about memory/knowledge.
asi.label_evidence: fixture shows url_reference noise=6 missed=0 and surreal_memory noise=7 missed=0
asi.next_action_hint: target remaining leak classes: curiosity://knowledge-gaps (6 leaks, currently unranked synthetic candidate), kb://journal historical memory (13 noise/0 missed), inquirer_memory (3/0), and file_snippet vs file preference (382 noise/0 missed for file_snippet)

description: Treat tool-state dot-directories as global noise (nvm, roo, antigravity, mtplx, 41d, .pi/understand-anything) + regression test.

asi.discovery: tool-state dot-directories account for ~12 of the remaining 52 top-3 noise leaks; the file_snippet artifact class is almost always noise on this corpus (noise=382, missed=0)
asi.generality: extends the existing enumerated GLOBAL_NOISY_SOURCE_PATTERNS list (.bun, .cdk/cache, .fallow, .pi/revolver) with more tool-state dirs; dev hold-out improved in the same direction (0.686 -> 0.557), which argues against pure fixture fitting, but the dir list is still machine-specific and should be reviewed before publishing
asi.hypothesis: Tool-state dot-directories (nvm, roo, antigravity, mtplx, 41d, .pi/understand-anything) are never project context and leak into top-3 as file_snippet noise.
asi.next_action_hint: remaining leaks: knowledge_gap 6, project_memory journal/wiki 5, self-artifacts 11+3, file_snippet home-root clutter, inquirer 2, doc_snippet 2; also watch empty_top_rate now at 0.124

description: Defer curiosity knowledge-gap meta-candidate to end of processed list — no metric change.

asi.discovery: all 6 knowledge_gap noise leaks are thin-pool cases (ranked out.length < 3), so deferring the gap still leaves it in top-3; 42/242 cases have a gap in top-3 and 30/242 have an empty top after filtering
asi.hypothesis: Synthetic curiosity://knowledge-gaps meta-candidate should never outrank source-grounded context in top-3, so defer it to the end of the processed list.
asi.result: metric unchanged (0.5433); deferral only helps when >=3 real items survive, which is not where the labeled leaks occur
asi.next_action_hint: thin-pool cases dominate the remaining failures: either raise recall by keeping one floor-quality candidate when filtering empties the pool, or attack the specific remaining noise classes (self-artifacts 15, project_memory 5, home-root file_snippet 6)

description: Require explicit historical intent (drop bare 'session') before historical journal memory is eligible.

asi.discovery: bare 'session' matched generic prompts about the current session, so journal entries leaked; explicit historical phrasing still admits real history prompts
asi.hypothesis: focusAllowsHistoricalMemory matched bare 'session', which most prompts mention; tightening it to explicit historical intent stops journal entries leaking as noise.
asi.next_action_hint: remaining leak classes: self-artifacts 15 (mostly prompts that mention the tool by name, so focus gating cannot fix them), project_memory wiki 2, home-root file_snippet 5, doc_snippet 2, inquirer 2; empty_top_rate now 0.128

description: Focus-gate runtime log sources (.pi/loops run logs+specs, .pi-memory/sherpa-traces) so they only surface for log/trace/metrics/loop prompts.

asi.discovery: runtime log artifacts (.pi/loops, .pi-memory/sherpa-traces) leak into top-3 on prompts that merely paste tool output; they need the same focus gating as other diagnostic classes
asi.hypothesis: Sherpa/Pi runtime logs (loop run logs, loop specs, retrieval traces) are diagnostic artifacts and should only be injected when the prompt asks about logs/traces/metrics/loops.
asi.next_action_hint: remaining: self-artifacts 15 (prompts often name the tool, so keyword gating cannot fix), project_memory wiki 2, home-root file_snippet 5, doc_snippet 2, inquirer 2; also tested and rejected the empty-pool fallback (would gain +1 missed pair but leak +6 noise pairs)

description: Allow package manifests whose own package directory is named in the prompt, instead of requiring generic dependency keywords.

asi.discovery: package manifests were being filtered out on code prompts even when the prompt named the package itself; the dev split improved in the same direction (missed_hit_dev 0.636 -> 0.727), a strong generalization signal
asi.hypothesis: A package manifest is on-topic when the prompt names its own package directory (e.g. focus mentions tdd_loop and candidate is .../tdd_loop/package.json), even without generic dependency keywords.
asi.next_action_hint: next recall bucket: doc_snippet items (census noise=3 vs missed=26) lose to file/pi_extension_file via the -0.25 wantsSource penalty; verify unique-label count before touching the penalty to avoid overfitting to one repeated research note

description: Require query-target lexical overlap for kb:// project_memory candidates (zero-overlap notes dropped).

asi.discovery: 596 project_memory candidate instances in the fixture; 449 had zero query-target overlap, of which 12 were human-labeled noise and 0 were labeled missed
asi.hypothesis: kb:// durable memory notes with no lexical connection to the prompt are precision risk and can be dropped; semantic recall is handled upstream by the vector/inquirer stage.
asi.next_action_hint: empty_top_rate rose to 0.157 (+22.6%) as a side effect - verify on real use that zero-overlap kb memory is genuinely useless before publishing; remaining leaks are mostly pasted-log self-artifacts that resist keyword gating

description: Drop generic terms (context, tag/tags) from inquirer memory gating + regression test.

asi.discovery: both inquirer leaks matched only the generic term 'context' in pasted error blobs; empty-pool audit at 38 cases shows 2 missed pairs vs 53 noise pairs, so stricter filtering is still correct, not a recall regression
asi.hypothesis: 'context' and 'tag/tags' are generic coding words, not memory-retrieval intent, and let vector inquirer memory into pasted-error prompts.
asi.next_action_hint: remaining leaks are pasted-log self-artifacts (pi-sherpa/index.ts, archivist/index.ts) whose prompts name the tool; a principled fix needs an intent signal rather than more keyword gating. Also consider svg/asset and self-config (.pi/sherpa.config.json) junk classes for a final small win

description: Suppress image/binary assets globally, gate Sherpa's own config to Sherpa prompts, and drop bare-directory file_exact candidates.

asi.discovery: three small junk classes each had exactly 1 noise label and 0 missed labels: image assets, Sherpa's own config, and bare-directory file_exact candidates
asi.hypothesis: Image/binary assets, Sherpa's own .pi/sherpa.config.json, and bare-directory file_exact candidates are never useful text context and can be suppressed without recall cost.
asi.rejected_hypothesis: pasted-log-blob detection for self-artifacts: in log-blob focuses self-artifact candidates are missed 26 vs noise 42, so suppressing them would cost 0.45 missed_hit for 0.31 noise_leak - net worse
asi.next_action_hint: primary metric now 0.4285; recall at label ceiling and remaining precision leaks are minority self-artifacts. Consider consolidating the noise-filter list for publishability and reviewing machine-specific dirs before packaging

description: Cap 2 items per directory in the ranked output (context diversity) + ranking regression test.

asi.discovery: 13 cases had all three top slots from one parent directory and the third item was never label-relevant; capping same-dir items promotes the next different-directory candidate
asi.hypothesis: Context diversity: spending all top slots on one directory wastes the budget; capping 2 items per directory (extras kept but pushed back) should promote other sources without losing anything.
asi.next_action_hint: primary metric 0.4113; recall residual is the 3 repeated docs and precision residual is minority self-artifacts, both label-ceiling limited. Stop benchmark tuning; next real steps are publishability cleanup (machine-specific noise dirs), re-baselining on fresh traces, and the open package-install decision

description: Treat foreign agent state (.claude/) as global noise and drop bare-directory file/file_snippet candidates.

asi.discovery: rejected a tempting knowledge_gap win as benchmark-gaming: dropping gaps in postProcessCandidates would score better but resolveModelFilterPool re-admits raw candidates when the filtered pool empties, so real thin-pool behavior would be unchanged
asi.hypothesis: Foreign agent tooling state (.claude/) is not project context, and file/file_snippet candidates that point at a bare directory (no filename) carry no content.
asi.next_action_hint: primary 0.4040; empty_top_rate 0.178 (verified twice: empty pools contain ~2 missed vs ~53 noise pairs, so filtering is correct). Remaining leaks are knowledge_gap thin pools (would be gaming to fix), repeated-doc recall, and self-artifacts the labels say are wanted elsewhere. Stop benchmark tuning; move to publishability cleanup and a fresh-trace re-baseline

description: Try removing/restricting the doc_snippet ranking penalty (KB docs missed 23 vs noise 3) — no metric change, root cause is upstream relevance.

asi.discovery: the doc_snippet penalty only applies when wantsSource (isCodePrompt/isSourceLookupPrompt) is true, and every unhit doc_snippet miss occurs in non-code prompts such as 'review pi-sherpa context curation quality'; the penalty never binds, so removing it changes nothing
asi.hypothesis: The -0.25 doc_snippet wantsSource penalty is miscalibrated (KB docs labeled missed 23 vs noise 3) and should be removed or restricted to in-repo docs.
rejected_variants: external-knowledge-only exemption (helper did not match repo://Documents/... relative paths)
full penalty removal (no-op for the miss cases, no noise change for code prompts)
asi.next_action_hint: the binding constraint for doc_snippet misses is the base retrieval relevance (0.45 vs 0.74-1.0 for competing files), i.e. upstream candidate scoring, not the ranking penalty; ranking-side levers are exhausted

description: Require an explicit Sherpa mention before injecting Sherpa retrieval traces + ranking regression tests.

asi.discovery: the 3 remaining sherpa-trace leaks matched generic terms (log, trace provenance, bundle/loop) in prompts about other systems; requiring an explicit sherpa mention removes 2 of 3 while the one genuinely sherpa-specific case stays
asi.hypothesis: Sherpa's own retrieval traces are only meaningful for Sherpa-specific diagnostics; generic 'logs' or 'trace provenance' prompts concern other systems.
asi.next_action_hint: primary 0.3967; empty_top_rate 0.194 (still verified as correct filtering). Remaining ranking leaks are knowledge_gap thin pools (fixing would be gaming via resolveModelFilterPool) and self-artifacts the labels say are wanted elsewhere; ranking-side is exhausted, pivot to a candidate-generation benchmark for upstream_miss_rate=0.93

description: Give pi_extension_file the same code-file ranking bonus as repo files — no metric change.

asi.discovery: pi_extension_file candidates already rank first in every case where they appear, so the code-file bonus changes nothing; pre-checked label census shows pi_extension_file is noise=0 missed=40, so it is valuable but not under-ranked
asi.hypothesis: Extension source files (pi_extension_file) are code and should receive the same wantsSource +0.35 preference as repo files.
asi.next_action_hint: third consecutive ranking no-op; ranking stage has no measurable headroom left. The remaining failures are upstream candidate generation (upstream_miss_rate=0.93) and would require a NEW benchmark axis plus init_experiment, not more ranking tweaks

description: Focus-gate agent metadata indexes (catalog.csv, routes.csv/md) + ranking regression tests.

asi.discovery: catalog.csv/routes.csv/routes.md are agent-managed wiring files: 5 noise-labeled instances, 0 missed; also found 11 file_snippets in top-3 of which only 4 are noise-labeled, so a file_snippet penalty would mostly remove unlabeled items
asi.hypothesis: Agent-managed index/route tables (memory catalog, extension route map) describe the agent's own wiring, not the user's project, so they need focus gating like other self-artifacts.
asi.next_action_hint: primary 0.3748; dev noise_leak improved to 0.129. Remaining leaks: knowledge_gap thin pools (gaming to fix), pasted-log self-artifacts (labels say wanted elsewhere), generate-bonsai-image.sh and catalog leftovers now gated. Ranking genuinely near ceiling

description: Focus-gate SKILL.md instruction files — no metric change (leaking prompts contain a 'Required skills:' section).

asi.discovery: the two leaking SKILL.md files appear in prompts that contain a 'Required skills:' section listing skill paths, so a keyword gate always allows them; the same prompts explicitly mention the leaking skill file yet the human still labeled it noise, so intent and mention cannot be separated with the current signals
asi.hypothesis: SKILL.md is the agent's own operating instruction and should only be injected when the prompt is about skills, not as general project knowledge.
asi.next_action_hint: 4th consecutive ranking no-op/negative; all remaining leak classes are (a) knowledge_gap thin pools, (b) self-artifacts in prompts that name the tool, or (c) repeated/contradictory doc labels. Honest ranking headroom is exhausted; the only productive path is the candidate-generation benchmark (needs init_experiment) or the pending package-install decision

description: Defer pi_extension_route stubs behind content-bearing candidates + ranking regression test.

asi.discovery: simulated the change before coding it: deferring pi_extension_route to the end of the processed list predicted label_loss 0.333 / missed_hit 0.828 / noise_leak 0.161, and the real run matched exactly
asi.hypothesis: Directory/route stubs are pointers, not content; they should never outrank content-bearing candidates (files, docs, memory) in the top slots, but should remain available when nothing else matches.
asi.next_action_hint: primary 0.3330; recall 0.828. This confirms a general principle: content-bearing items outrank pointer/synthetic items. Check whether the same deferral helps other pointer classes (sherpa_trace_location, memory_index) via simulation before coding

description: Kind diversity: cap code-type candidates at 2 of the top slots when a non-code candidate exists + regression test.

asi.caveat: gains trace to 2 unique docs (one is the repeated fix-sherpa research note); the rule is structural (kind diversity) rather than a doc boost, and the hold-out split improved strongly in the same direction (missed_hit_dev 0.727 -> 0.909), which argues against pure fixture fitting
asi.discovery: simulation matrix showed no single-type deferral helps (sherpa_trace_location worse, memory_index/git_status/file_snippet/knowledge_gap neutral), but capping the code kind to 2 of the top slots lets a relevant knowledge item enter without a blanket knowledge-first reorder
asi.first_attempt: unconditional code-kind cap broke the directory-diversity regression test on all-code pools; fixed by only applying the kind cap when a non-code candidate exists
asi.hypothesis: Context diversity should apply to kind, not just directory: code candidates must not monopolize all top slots when a relevant knowledge candidate is available.
asi.next_action_hint: primary 0.2322, recall 0.914, dev 0.220. Remaining misses are mostly the repeated docs now in top-3; remaining leaks are knowledge_gap thin pools and named self-artifacts. This is likely the practical ceiling of the ranking metric

description: Cap durable-memory artifacts at one front slot — no metric change (simulation harness bug produced a false prediction).

asi.discovery: my simulation helper was buggy: capBy(fn, cap) applied the cap to every key, not just the target type, so 'cap project_memory at 1' actually capped all other types at 1 too and produced a false 0.2150 prediction; the real single-pass and two-pass memory-kind caps both measure 0.2322 (no-op)
asi.hypothesis: Durable-memory artifacts (project_memory/research_memory/inquirer_memory) are never labeled missed (project_memory: noise 13x, missed 0x) and should be capped at one in the front slots.
asi.next_action_hint: verify simulation transforms reproduce the intended rule before coding (e.g. assert the transform's output differs from identity on a synthetic pool); ranking metric likely at its practical ceiling at 0.2322
